news.title: Football: Soccer-FIFA to visit potential 2030 World Cup host cities in November and December
news.lede: Oct 27 (Reuters) - FIFA ⁠will carry out a series of visits to ⁠candidate host cities in Spain, Portugal and Morocco ‌in November and December as part of the venue selection process for the 2030 World Cup, world football's governing body said on Tuesday. A ​FIFA delegation will visit candidate cities ⁠and stadiums in all ⁠three host countries to assess their suitability to host ⁠games. FIFA ‌has yet to confirm which venues will be included, and has not announced where the ⁠World Cup final will be held, withSpain and ​Morocco battling ‌to hold football's biggest match. Visits are planned forAgadir, Casablanca, ⁠Fez, Marrakech, ​Rabat and Tangier in Morocco; Lisbon and Porto in Portugal; and Barcelona, Bilbao, Las Palmas, Madrid, San Sebastian, Seville ⁠and Zaragoza in Spain.FIFA said it ​may also conduct visits to additional venues during the selection process.

news.title: Uzbekistan U-15 Finish Second in World Cup Group
news.lede: Tashkent, Uzbekistan (UzDaily.uz) — Uzbekistan’s under-15 national team finished second in Group W at the FIFA U-15 World Cup & Festival 2026 in Baku and will now compete for the Level B title. The team’s next match is scheduled for 28 October against Guatemala, the Uzbekistan Football Association reported. Under the tournament format, teams advance after the group stage to compete across six levels: A, B, C, D, E and F. Each level has its own winner, while the Level A winner will be crowned the overall tournament champion.

news.title: 2030 World Cup: Morocco prepares a package of tax exemptions for FIFA
news.lede: Special tax regime for FIFA Benefits and beneficiaries 2030 World Cup Legacy Fund Morocco’s draft finance bill for 2027 provides for a package of tax and customs exemptions for FIFA and the organisations involved in organising the 2030 World Cup, which the country will co-host with Spain and Portugal. The measures include tax benefits for organisations, suppliers and other participants linked to the tournament, with the aim of facilitating the preparations and running of the competition. The initiative seeks to fulfil the financial and legal commitments undertaken by Morocco towards FIFA through a specific tax regime for activities related to the tournament. news.title: Inaugural FIFA U-15 World Cup & Festival kicks off in Azerbaijan
news.lede: A new era for international youth football has arrived as the inaugural FIFA U-15 World Cup & Festival officially kicked off in Baku, Azerbaijan. The historic tournament brings together thousands of aspiring players for a unique competition designed to provide a global stage for the next generation of stars. The groundbreaking competition features more than 3,000 players and officials representing 189 member associations, highlighting an unprecedented level of inclusivity in the international game, with as many as 78 of the nations participating in the tournament having never previously been represented at any FIFA World Cup level. Speaking at the opening ceremony, FIFA President Gianni Infantino - joined by Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev - emphasised the symbolic and practical importance of creating a pathway for young athletes from every corner of the planet.
